issue_context.title: systemd-networkd: Cannot create vlan network on SR-IOV VF after recent update
issue_context.body:
Hello, I am on Arch Linux 5.17.37-1-lts:

```
# systemctl --version
systemd 250 (250.5-1-arch)
```

~~I think this began with the upgrade from 250.4 to 250.5 but I am not sure.~~

The update was from 249.5-1 to 250.5-1:

```
[2022-05-05T23:36:54+0300] [ALPM] upgraded systemd-libs (249.5-1 -> 250.5-1)
[2022-05-05T23:36:55+0300] [ALPM] upgraded systemd (249.5-1 -> 250.5-1)
[2022-05-05T23:38:07+0300] [ALPM] upgraded systemd-sysvcompat (249.5-1 -> 250.5-1)
```

I am unable to create vlan networks on SR-IOV VF interfaces. I am using SR-IOV VFs and their VLAN networks for docker networking on the host. Journalctl shows this error:

```
May 08 23:36:27 hostname systemd-networkd[3798258]: eno1v16: Could not create stacked netdev: Input/output error
May 08 23:36:27 hostname systemd-networkd[3798258]: eno1v16: Failed
```

Manually creating the vlan interface with:

```
ip link add link eno1v16 name eno1v16.400 type vlan id 400
```

works as expected. The interface gets created and is functional.
comments:
Please provide relevant .network, .netdev, and .link files. Also, please provide debugging logs of networkd, it can be generated by creating the following drop-in config:
```
# /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
Environment=SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
```

```
# cat eno1v16.400.netdev 
[NetDev]
Name=eno1v16.400
Kind=vlan

[VLAN]
Id=400
```

```
# cat eno1v16.network 
[Match]
Name=eno1v16

[Network]
VLAN=eno1v16.400
```

```
# cat eno1v15.200.netdev 
[NetDev]
Name=eno1v15.200
Kind=vlan

[VLAN]
Id=200
```

```
# cat eno1v15.network 
[Match]
Name=eno1v15

[Network]
VLAN=eno1v15.200
```

```
# cat eno1v26.400.netdev
[NetDev]
Name=eno1v26.400
Kind=vlan

[VLAN]
Id=400
```

```
# cat eno1v26.network 
[Match]
Name=eno1v26

[Network]
VLAN=eno1v26.400
```

journalctl pastebin: https://pastebin.com/5nugiNDJ

@sotiris-bos Thank you for the logs and configs.

The error seems to be caused when the main interface become down state during a vlan netdev is added to the virtual interface, though I cannot found the error path which returns `-EIO` in the kernel.

Hence, it is a race in configuring the physical interface and virtual interfaces. This should not be a new issue, and potentially happens on older release. The issue just becomes apparent on a recent release.
Downgrading the label from 'regression' to 'bug'.

Please reconfigure failed interfaces with `networkctl reconfigure eno1v26` until it is solved.

@sotiris-bos Could you show the results of the following??
```
udevadm info --attribute-walk /sys/class/net/eno1v26
udevadm info --attribute-walk /sys/class/net/eno1
```

@sotiris-bos There should be multiple ways. I usually use the following:
```
# install development tools like gcc, meson, ninja, etc
$ cd
$ git clone git@github.com:systemd/systemd.git
$ cd systemd
$ git remote add yuwata git@github.com:yuwata/systemd.git
$ git fetch yuwata network-check-sr-iov-pf-state
$ git checkout network-check-sr-iov-pf-state
$ sudo mkdir /var/systemd-build
$ sudo chown USERNAME:GROUPNAME /var/systemd-build
$ cd /var/systemd-build
$ meson . ~/systemd
$ ninja
$ sudo systemctl edit systemd-networkd.service
$ cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=/var/systemd-build/systemd-networkd
Environment=SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
$ sudo systemctl restart systemd-networkd.service
```
Then, you can use the patched networkd without installing it. When you want to use the currently installed networkd again, then please use `systemctl revert systemd-networkd.service`.

One of the important point in the above step is that you need to build systemd somewhere everyone can read, e.g. /var/systemd-build/. Or, if it cannot, and you need to build systemd under your home directory, then please disable several protections enabled in systemd-networkd.service, at least `ProtectHome=no` is necessary.
